text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The paper says in its editorial that political parties will not find a way out of the present crisis if they continue to refuse to talk to each other.

- Trial of Albania's last communist president Ramiz Alia and four other senior officials, charged with crimes against humanity, was postponed on Tuesday after the presiding judge said the appeals court would have to rule on a call by Alia's lawyer for new judges to be appointed.
- U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said Europe and the U.S. should take a similar stand on recent events in Albania.
- President Sali Berisha held a meeting with his supporters in the southern town of Lushnje, repeating his stand on the present crisis.
- The opposition Forum for Democracy alliance supported calls by Vlore local officials for the government to step down.
- World Bank representative in Albania, Carlos Elbirt, denied the international organisation would financially support Albania to overcome its present crisis.
- Prices are rising even though official statistics show inflation is stable.
- Value of privatisation vouchers distributed by the government has been reduced to 2.5 percent of their face value.

- A group of 100 intellectuals in Vlore threatened to go on hunger strike on Thursday unless the government fulfilled their demand for the return of capital invested in a failed pyramid investment scheme.
- Vlore women's basketball team refuses to play matches to express their solidarity with local protesters.

- President Sali Berisha said on Tuesday residents in the southern region would not have to pay taxes for two years to help them recover from the loss of large sums of money in fraudulent pyramid investment schemes.
- Opposition Forum for Democracy invited exiled King Leka to come to the country to help resolve the crisis.
- Berisha ordered army units, which had been deployed to assist police forces in the restoration of the public order, to withdraw to their barracks.
